column2: On the authority of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him), from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:

“If you were to rely on Allah as He truly deserves to be relied upon, He would provide for you as He provides for the birds: they go out in the morning with empty stomachs and return in the evening with full stomachs.” Reported by Imam Aḥmad, al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī, Ibn Mājah, Ibn Ḥibbān and al-Ḥākim; al-Tirmidhī said: Ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.

“As He truly deserves to be relied upon”: by depending on Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and no one else, in bringing about benefits and warding off harms in matters of this world and the Hereafter, with faith that none but Allah the Exalted gives, withholds or benefits.
Khimāṣan (“with empty stomachs”): lean-bellied from hunger.
Tarūḥu (“return in the evening”): come back at the end of the day,
biṭānan (“with full stomachs”): with filled bellies.

The virtue of reliance [on Allah], and that it is among the greatest means by which provision is brought; Allah the Exalted said: “And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him” [al-Ṭalāq 65:3].
Reliance does not contradict attending to means, for he informed us that true reliance is not opposed by going out in the morning and returning in the evening in search of provision.

That is why Imam Aḥmad was asked about a man who sat in his house or in the mosque and said, “I will not do anything until my provision comes to me.” Aḥmad said: “This is a man ignorant of knowledge”, and he cited this hadith as evidence.
